sections.title: Writing: A letter to the editor

questions.prompt: Write your own 200–250 word letter to the editor responding to the article.
questions.response:
Dear editor,

I am writing in response to your article entitled "An in depth look at the surprising nautical origins of Giza's ancient wonders" from National Geographic.

While I recognise that the pyramids are very mysterious, I am not entirely convinced by the mystical theories. In my opinion, the scientific explanation seems more believable.

Furthermore, your article presents two important details. First, you explain that the Giza plateau perhaps bordered a bustling harbor on a lost branch of the Nile and that it might have been a marine-industrial project. I believe this makes sense because the diary of inspector Merer, written many years ago (4,600) and discovered in 2013, documented intact stones sliding down river in boats. This could show how they transported heavy weight by water. Second, you mentioned that each stone weighs as much as a minivan and the granite slabs over Khufu's chamber are heavier than semitrucks. Joseph Davidovits proposed that blocks were cast from limestone slurry in baskets, but your article says granite is undeniably natural and harder to fabricate, so it appears his idea may not be correct.

Nevertheless, I understand another viewpoint. Edgar Cayce, the Sleeping Prophet, said that people from Atlantis built the pyramids around 10,500 B.C. by levitation and buried a hall of records under the right forepaw of the Sphinx. To some extent, this story is interesting because moving so much material seems impossible.

I would therefore argue that we should trust evidence-based research like Mark Lehner's work. I would suggested that you publish more studies about this lost harbor.

Yours faithfully,
Fernanda Issabella Mercado González.

yours faithfully,
